[h1]Fun and challenging — an excellent game![/h1]
[h2]What I liked:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Brilliant implementation of shooting mechanics and weapon handling. I loved how aiming and cover are designed.
[*]The locations are both beautiful and functional — you can almost always fight enemies at the distance that best suits your playstyle.
[*]The sound design feels like an extension of your eyes! If a skirmish breaks out nearby, you can clearly identify who’s involved, how many opponents there are, and what weapons they’re using.
[*]The bosses are amusing (: Some of them will obliterate you instantly if you’re not prepared (:
[*]I really enjoyed the game’s difficulty curve. I could feel myself growing as a player, yet I was always aware that I could still be destroyed in a second if I got careless or overconfident. I also liked how deadly the player becomes by the end of the game (:
[/list]
[h2]What I didn’t like:[/h2]
[list]
[*]The last quarter of the game suffered from randomness — keycards required to access certain rooms dropped inconsistently (and at least one was needed to complete a quest).
[*]I wasn’t impressed by the melee combat. I tried a lot of different options, but melee always felt inferior to any ranged weapon. Its only real advantage is that it lets you live out the classic Counter-Strike meme — you run faster with a knife ((:
[/list]

Escape from Duckov is a surprisingly fun and engaging game that plunges you into a hostile, duck-filled world. Starting from nothing, the core gameplay loop is immediately engaging: you scavenge for resources, build your hideout, and upgrade your gear to survive.

What truly makes the game shine is the depth of its progression. The randomized drops keep the necessary looting fresh and exciting, while the array of unlockables and level-ups ensures you always have a goal in sight. If you enjoy survival games where the maps get progressively harder, forcing you to constantly adapt your strategy and refine your gear, this indie title is a must-play. It offers a deeply satisfying, randomized grind that feels new every time you go out into the various maps.

This is one of those single player games that is so good that it puts all of your other aspirations and responsibilities at risk of not getting done. This game is for those who just want to enjoy playing a game again without the same game-ruining issues that plagues modern online gaming. What may seem like a bizarre concept at first is extremely fun, surprisingly complex, and has just as much difficulty and stress as you want at any given time. Games like Escape from Duckov break the already tired mold of extraction shooters and makes it fun again. It can suck you in for hours or serve as quick session of rewarding game play. This is a game that sticks a big middle finger to the AAA titles from publishers that have too much power and influence over the gaming industry. The same old ideas are recycled endlessly by companies like Activision, EA, and Ubisoft, all while asking for more and more of people's money just for the right to play broken products. Helldivers 2, Duckov, and even Arc Raiders are modern examples of AAA quality games by fresh blood in the industry at a price point that is accessible to all - the way gaming should be.

Tarkov introduced me to the extraction shooter and gave me an itch that it could never quite fully scratch. It was always a little too tedious or grindy or filled with questionable moments. I messed around with the SP Tarkov mod trying to find a fix but nope.

That itch kinda died and hid away until I saw Duckov on the store. Man did it scratch it. Duckov captures the spirit and feel of Tarkov but stays light hearted and "easy" enough to keep you engaged. At first glance, it's a parody that probably shouldn't be taken seriously but it is a serious game with its own flavor and take on concepts (and alot of lore) that Tarkov introduced.

If your even slightly intrigued, give it a go.

This game is pure frustration.  Every mission is a fetch quest or "Kill X person with Y specific weapon you have to grind more to get."  You collect tons of vendor trash, but don't know what you need to save to complete future missions, and have very limited backpack and storage space.  There are few maps, and they are poorly designed, with lots of blind corners leading no where and endless backtracking.  The baseline "normal" difficulty is very difficult.  (Though you can customize it to lower the difficulty as much as you want, this turns off achievements).  By default if you're killed and don't retrieve your stuff from the map on the first try, you lose your items (with limited safety boxes on your pet dog), and thus can lose a lot of your progression.  It seems like this game is targeted to a very specific fandom of players who like insanely difficult survival games.  But if you're a casual player like me who stumbled across it and bought it because it had a lot of positive buzz online, you will be deeply disappointed in your purchase.  I kept playing until I beat it, thinking it would somehow get better, but it does not.  Endless grind.  Do not buy this game unless you've played other similar survival crafting games and love the genre.

A top-down, cartoony survival shooter with an addictive gameplay loop—featuring incredibly satisfying gunplay, real tension, and above all, the brilliant idea of a “top-down extraction shooter lite.” Pure genius.

As a dev myself I think the world of extraction games is ripe for some truly great indie titles.
